         loader = FileSystemLoader(["/override/templates", "/default/templates"])
 
+    Each item in the list can also be a ``(path, priority)`` tuple to
+    control the search order independently of the order the paths are
+    listed in. Paths with a higher priority are searched first. Paths
+    that are given without a priority have a priority of ``0``, and
+    priorities may be negative to search a path after the default ones.
+    Paths with the same priority are searched in the order they were
+    given.
+
+    .. code-block:: python
+
+        loader = FileSystemLoader([
+            ("/high/priority/themes", 100),   # searched first
+            ("/medium/priority/plugins", 50),  # searched second
+            "/default/templates",              # priority 0, searched third
+            ("/low/priority/fallback", -10),   # searched last
+        ])
+
+    Regular paths and ``(path, priority)`` tuples can be mixed.
+
+    .. code-block:: python
+
+        loader = FileSystemLoader([
+            "/regular/path",           # priority 0
+            ("/priority/path", 75),    # priority 75, searched first
+            "/another/regular/path",   # priority 0
+        ])
+
     :param searchpath: A path, or list of paths, to the directory that
-        contains the templates.
+        contains the templates. Each item may be a path or a
+        ``(path, priority)`` tuple. Higher priorities are searched
+        first, and the default priority is ``0``.
     :param encoding: Use this encoding to read the text from template
         files.
     :param followlinks: Follow symbolic links in the path.
 
+    .. versionchanged:: 3.1
+        Paths can be given as ``(path, priority)`` tuples to control
+        the order they are searched in.
+
     .. versionchanged:: 2.8
         Added the ``followlinks`` parameter.
+
+    .. versionchanged:: 3.1
+        The path each template name resolves to is cached, including
+        names that were not found, so repeated lookups skip the search
+        of ``searchpath``.
     """
 
     def __init__(
         self,
-        searchpath: t.Union[str, os.PathLike, t.Sequence[t.Union[str, os.PathLike]]],
+        searchpath: t.Union[
+            str,
+            os.PathLike,
+            t.Sequence[
+                t.Union[str, os.PathLike, t.Tuple[t.Union[str, os.PathLike], int]]
+            ],
+        ],
         encoding: str = "utf-8",
         followlinks: bool = False,
     ) -> None:
         if not isinstance(searchpath, abc.Iterable) or isinstance(searchpath, str):
             searchpath = [searchpath]
 
-        self.searchpath = [os.fspath(p) for p in searchpath]
+        # Items are a path or a (path, priority) tuple. Anything else is
+        # treated as a path with the default priority, so an invalid item
+        # fails in os.fspath as it always has.
+        path_priorities: t.List[t.Tuple[str, int]] = []
+
+        for item in searchpath:
+            if isinstance(item, tuple) and len(item) == 2:
+                path, priority = item
+                path_priorities.append((os.fspath(path), priority))
+            else:
+                path_priorities.append((os.fspath(item), 0))
+
+        # The sort is stable, even in reverse, so paths with the same
+        # priority keep the order they were given in.
+        path_priorities.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[1], reverse=True)
+        self.searchpath = [path for path, _ in path_priorities]
         self.encoding = encoding
         self.followlinks = followlinks
+        # Maps a template name to the path it resolved to, or to None
+        # when the name was searched for and not found.
+        self._path_cache: t.Dict[str, t.Optional[str]] = {}
+
+    def _read_source(
+        self, f: t.BinaryIO, filename: str
+    ) -> t.Tuple[str, str, t.Callable[[], bool]]:
+        try:
+            contents = f.read().decode(self.encoding)
+        finally:
+            f.close()
+
+        mtime = os.path.getmtime(filename)
+
+        def uptodate() -> bool:
+            try:
+                return os.path.getmtime(filename) == mtime
+            except OSError:
+                return False
+
+        return contents, filename, uptodate
 
     def get_source(
         self, environment: "Environment", template: str
     ) -> t.Tuple[str, str, t.Callable[[], bool]]:
+        if template in self._path_cache:
+            cached = self._path_cache[template]
+
+            if cached is None:
+                raise TemplateNotFound(template)
+
+            f = open_if_exists(cached)
+
+            if f is not None:
+                return self._read_source(f, cached)
+
+            # The file is gone, so resolve the name again from scratch.
+            del self._path_cache[template]
+
